reviews.text:
If you stay at Little Riverside Hotel, don’t miss the chance to explore the nearby riverbank area — it’s quiet, local, and full of gentle charm.

In the morning, you’ll see locals riding bicycles, vendors setting up, and the soft mist rising from the Thu Bon River. The pace is calm, almost meditative. You can walk along the narrow streets, spot elegant shop signs, and pass by cafés that haven’t opened yet — it feels like Hội An before the crowds.

Tip: Wake up a little early, bring a camera, and just follow the river. No plan needed.

Lucky was such an amazing tour guide with a wealth of information. She was really great at speaking English and carrying a meaningful conversation with us the entire time. She had so much knowledge about the food and local history. We are so grateful to have had Lucky as our tour guide! We were also SO FULL after our tour, so make sure to go on an empty stomach!

Sam Rocks! , Delicious food tour. Egg Coffee and the Banh Mi were my favorite. I found Sam on YouTube and she didn’t disappoint 😎We did the morning tour so we couldn’t dive in to the heavy duty food, and we were still full.

Got the chance to go on this food tour with Sam today. I’m so glad I did. It was just me and her. I can be a little shy but she made me feel comfortable. She is really nice and made sure I was safe while walking in these crazy streets. The food options were great and diverse. Personally my favorite was the chicken and rice (COM GA). And the Sesame soup. I was really impressed buy how much I liked it since I’m not much of a dessert person. I got to meet some of the local workers and joke around with them. Overall great experience. You should totally book this tour! 🩷

We had the best private walking street food tour with our guide, Lucky! We got to try about eight different dishes, and Lucky was able to cater to our needs and allergies of group members. We got to try a range of items including beverages, small plates, main dishes and dessert at high quality local restaurants and road side shops. Her knowledge as a Hoi An local meant she could answer any questions we had! & make sure you go on an empty stomach 😁

Lucky, our tour guide, took us on a fantastic private tour of the streets of Hoi An. She gave us an insightful look into the lives and culture of the people and food of Hoi An. We went to places that we would never have known about without the tour. We didn't want to be a part of a large tour group, so the private tour was perfect for us and at a very reasonable price.
Lucky also gave us tips about places to visit on our own in the days following which were fabulous. Booking Hoi An Street Food Tours is a must when visiting Hoi An! 10/10.
Sam has been a great guide. We were so full at the end of the tour hahahah. But food was delicious and we stopped at some places where we wouldn’t have had as tourists. Thanks again Sam!!!

I had a wonderful experience on my day trip to Mỹ Sơn Sanctuary. Everything was thoughtfully planned from start to finish. I received clear confirmation and pickup instructions ahead of time, and the driver made the journey feel safe and easy.

Our guide, Hiếu, was knowledgeable, helpful, and genuinely kind. I learned so much about the local culture and the deep history of the area. The sanctuary itself was magnificent, and the local lunch included on the tour was tasty and relaxing.

The group size was just right & not too big with a mix of solo travelers (like me) and pairs. From what I observed, everyone was treated kindly and taken care of. The boat ride down the river through Hoi An’s old town was such a lovely way to end the day before heading back to Da Nang.

I felt safe, inspired, and enriched throughout the entire experience. Highly recommend.

An absolutely fantastic tour of Hoi An with Jackie!
​If you're looking for a guide who is knowledgeable, fun, and truly passionate about the city, you need to book with Jackie. She made the history of Hoi An feel alive and vibrant, not just a series of facts.
​Jackie was incredible at navigating the Old Town efficiently, pointing out all the hidden gems and local secrets we would have missed on our own. She had a fantastic sense of humor and made everyone in our group feel comfortable and engaged. She even took some brilliant photos for us at the best spots!
​I highly recommend Jackie for anyone visiting Hoi An. Five stars all the way—she is a true professional and made this tour the highlight of my trip. Thank you, Jackie!

We booked this tour via Klook last minute and were expecting it to be a group tour, but it turned out to be just me and my friend — which was such a nice surprise. Our tour guide, TingTing, was very welcoming and easy to talk to. She explained all the spots in Hoi An clearly and shared interesting stories that made us appreciate the place even more. The transportation from Da Nang to Hoi An was smooth and convenient too. Overall, it was a comfortable, meaningful, and enjoyable experience. Highly recommended. 🙏✨

This was the perfect tour for anyone wanting a no frills experience of the My Son Sanctuary and temples. Emma was a fantastic guide, with great English and lots of knowledge about the specifics of the temples and their history. The banh mi and coffee on the way back was delicious. I highly recommend going at 5.30am as we did, as I can see how hot it gets out there! Thanks for the great experience.

Absolutely loved this tour, My Son is a must-visit. The temple grounds are so beautiful with the surrounding mountains, the chirping birds, and the awe-inspiring ancient structures. Our tour guide named Toàn was so friendly and informative, and I was fascinated to learn and ask about everything in My Son. Then we were given some of the best Banh Mi I’ve ever had and I got a perfect egg coffee at the tour’s end. Couldn’t recommend more, so fun!

Had an excellent guide, he was able to answer all the questions I had and I left the tour with a notebook full of intricate details about Mi Son and the history of Vietnam pre/post colonisation and pre/post war. He even suggested other experiences to build on my knowledge and I had no questions left by the end of the tour.

My Son Sanctuary was one of the places that pushed me to travel to Vietnam and I was not disappointed. The sanctuary is absolutely divine in itself but Toan was such an amazing guide that he made the experience even better. Interested, passionate and knowledgeable about the place and its history, Toan helped us re-enacting this civilisation from another time. Thank you so much !

The tour was informative and fun. Our guide Mr. Toan taught us a lot about the history and  some fun facts about My Son Sanctuary and the civilization that used to be here. After the tour at My Son, we went to eat bahn mi and drink coffee. Overall, it was good 😊💯

reviews.text: What a beautiful family experience. We attended without a booking when the shop was quiet and the ladies were so friendly, patient and helpful. Our family of 4 (kids 11 and 12) all made a lantern from scratch and were supported and guided along the way. It was a fun, unique experience, and all the staff ensured our lanterns were well made but allowed each of us to create and learn with their support. The kids love that they made their own souvenir. It was certainly one of our favourite Hoi An experiences.

Really friendly. No advance booking required. Really helpful if you’re not that experienced at crafts. A really cool idea and a perfect holiday souvenir or a great gift for friends.
Really enjoyed it; it’s definitely worth a visit!

We had a great morning making lanterns. Range of sizes, shapes and fabrics to choose from. You can opt to cover a pre-made lantern or make one from scratch. Hubby and my 7 year old did the pre-made and my 11 year old and I did from scratch which took longer. It was really busy when we were there but the staff were helpful and fixed any problems we had (ie cutting the string on the lantern a number of times - oops!). If you go during a busy time you will need to be patient.

We are so excited to display our one of a kind handmade souvenirs when we get home. It’s such an adorable activity and a meaningful item to take home - I’d highly recommend.

What a great find! Spent an amazing time with the family this morning making our own lanterns. We had no crafting experience but the owner and staff were so helpful teaching us along the way. Highlight of our trip to Hoi An!

If you’re visiting Hoi An, you absolutely have to experience The Lantern Lady workshop. It is honestly one of the best around. From the moment I arrived, the family made me feel so welcome — they are incredibly accommodating, kind, and genuinely passionate about what they do.

They guide you through every step of the lantern-making process with so much patience and care, making it both fun and easy to follow. I had such an amazing time learning how to make my own lantern from scratch, and being able to choose my own fabrics made the experience even more special. Creating something beautiful with your own hands, guided by such a lovely family, is truly unforgettable.

This isn’t just a workshop — it feels personal, authentic, and heartfelt. Definitely a must-do while you’re here!

We recently visited The Lantern Lady while staying in Hoi A with our 2 kids (ages 8 & 10) and we had such a great time experience! We went very much thinking that it would just be an activity for the kids but we ended up really enjoying it too. We got so much help and support and everyone really enjoyed the whole process. We were given space to take our time but also help when we needed it and it feels so special to have such a meaningful souvenir to bring home. Really glad we found such a great workshop! Thank you!

We went to the lantern lady without a booking and they managed to fit in my partner and I without any problems (Sunday afternoon). We both made our lanterns from the first step of building the frame and the staff carefully helped us at each part. We spent some time there and we are very happy with our lanterns! They are collapsible so we are able to take them with us on our travels. It's a lovely relaxing environment down a side street and the staff are warm and welcoming. I would highly recommend going to Lantern Lady!

With lanterns lighting up every corner of Hoi An, it’s tempting to just buy one and move on, but this experience lets you actually be part of it.

The staff were incredibly attentive and genuinely helpful. If you made a mistake, they didn’t just fix it for you, they showed you how to do it properly, which made the whole thing feel much more authentic. They guided us through each step without hovering, and were friendly the entire time.

You can customise everything - the shape, size, and fabric. You can either work with a pre-made frame or build the frame yourself if you want the full experience. Best part, the lanterns fold down to roughly the size of a drink bottle, so they’re easy to carry around all day or pack in your luggage.

Honestly considering going back for another one.

We had such a fantastic experience here and would highly recommend it to anyone visiting Hoi An.

We chose to visit at 1pm, which turned out to be perfect as it was the hottest part of the day. The workshop is fully air-conditioned, with cold drinks available to buy from the fridge, making it a brilliant way to escape the heat while doing something memorable.

We came as a family with our 4-year-old daughter and grandparents, and it was an activity that everyone could enjoy together. The ladies running the workshop were incredibly patient, kind and encouraging, taking the time to demonstrate every step and helping whenever we got stuck without ever making us feel rushed. They were especially wonderful with our daughter, making sure she was involved throughout, guiding her carefully at every stage and ensuring she was progressing and enjoying herself the whole time. It really made the experience feel inclusive for all ages.

There are two workshop options:
• A 45–60 minute session where you decorate a pre-made lantern frame with your chosen fabric.
• A 90-minute session where you build the bamboo lantern frame yourself before covering it with fabric.

There is a huge selection of beautiful fabrics to choose from, so every lantern feels unique.

One of the best features is that the lanterns are designed to collapse flat, so you can easily pack them into your suitcase and take home a beautiful handmade lantern.

This was one of our favourite activities in Hoi An: relaxing, creative, suitable for all ages, and a lovely way to spend a few hours together as a family. If you’re looking for something different from sightseeing, don’t miss this experience!

Onya Bike Tours – A Journey of a Lifetime

Touring Vietnam by motorcycle has been one of the greatest experiences of our lives.

From day one, we were warmly welcomed and thoroughly briefed on what to expect over the next seven days. The presentation was led by our group leader, Minh, along with his mechanic, Phong.

Our group of six riders ranged in age from our mid-30s to our late 60s, with varying levels of riding experience. Minh immediately put everyone at ease, assuring us that each rider would be capable of navigating every stage of the tour, while making it clear that safety was always his number one priority.

During the orientation, we were given a clear overview of each day’s ride while still leaving a few surprises for us to discover along the way. The evening before departure, we were fitted with our riding gear and provided with dry bags, bungee cords, and rain gear.

On the morning of departure, we inspected our motorcycles with the staff before setting off. At the end of every day, the bikes were checked, serviced, and prepared for the next day’s adventure, giving us complete confidence in the equipment.

The true highlight of this journey was Minh’s extensive knowledge of Vietnam’s history. He shared fascinating stories and insights into the country’s struggles, resilience, and remarkable journey to where it is today. Every historical site we visited was followed by an engaging explanation that brought each location to life. His passion for his country was evident and added tremendous value to the experience.

The riding itself was exceptionally well planned. We experienced stunning mountain vistas, winding roads, incredibly twisty sections, and relaxed scenic touring. It truly was a motorcyclist’s dream.

We do have a few suggestions that we believe would make an already excellent tour even better while adding another layer of safety:

* Equip the guides and riders with communication systems. Being connected to the guides—and to each other—would be especially valuable when navigating the busy and often chaotic traffic in the cities. At a minimum, both guides should have communication systems.
* Carry a small supply of miscellaneous repair items, such as visor hardware or basic helmet parts, to deal with minor equipment issues that can arise during a week-long tour.
* Replace some of the rain gear. Although it was worn correctly, several riders still became quite wet during heavy rain.
* Give guides the flexibility to recognize when a particular section of terrain may be beyond the comfort level of some riders and offer an alternate route when appropriate.
* Ensure the lead guide is equipped and trained to act as the initial responder should an emergency occur.

We also want to commend your entire team for the professionalism shown throughout the trip. The hotels were, in general, comfortable and well chosen. Minh consistently selected outstanding restaurants that showcased the unique flavours of each region while offering fresh, healthy, and authentic Vietnamese cuisine. Every meal was memorable.

Thank you to the entire Onya Bike Tours team for an unforgettable adventure.

On behalf of Paul, Gary, Nauris , Lauris, Brian, and Don—thank you for creating memories that will last a lifetime.

questionsAndAnswers.question: I want to know, is Hot Stone Massage and Aroma Massage in Hoi An different from Da Nang?

answers.answer:
Hot stone Massage: Combine the traditional massage method and use hot (warm) stones to apply to your body, use in combination with essential oils from lemongrass. Reduced muscle tension, reduced stress and anxiety, better sleep and better mental health.

Aroma Massage: Using natural herbal flavors, wrapped in cloth and rubbing on your body, combined with pure essential oils from lemongrass or coconut, or Vaseline (for sensitive skin). Purify your body and especially your skin. Helps skin look young and full of life. Stimulates blood vessels and increases the volume of red blood cells in the body.

Basically, massage in Hoi An or massage in Da Nang are the same. It only differs by the technique of the massage therapist.

I’ve had massages around the world and the aroma massage is unique to Vietnam. Highly recommend it! The dried herbs are wrapped in a cloth and are kind of “stamped” on your body and moved around in massaging motions. I find it similar but definitely distinct from the hot stone and hot bamboo massages.
Not sure as i did not have one at Da Nang

If you want to explore a traditional craft village and learn more about the local culture in Hoi An, Kim Bong Carpentry Village is definitely a destination worth experiencing.
When I came here, I had the chance to learn about the traditional carpentry craft that has been preserved through many generations. What I enjoyed the most was seeing the artisans carve, engrave, and shape wooden products by hand. Each product shows the skill, care, and dedication of the craftsmen. 🪵🔨
The most interesting experience was getting to try making a simple wooden product by myself, feeling how challenging each step was and understanding more about the value of the traditional carpentry craft. It was not only a fun activity but also helped me appreciate more the cultural values preserved in this craft village.
The village is peaceful, rustic, and close to nature, giving a completely different feeling from the busy atmosphere of Hoi An Ancient Town.
It was an experience that was both interesting and meaningful, especially suitable for those who love culture, traditional handicrafts, and want to discover a more peaceful side of Hoi An.

COLONIAL POSTAGE STAMPS – A GLIMPSE INTO WORLD HISTORY

This collection features rare antique postage stamps with distinctive gold-bronze embossed designs, reflecting the postal history of various territories and colonies around the world, including the Straits Settlements, India, Australia, Malta, Sudan, and Aden.

Portraits of kings and queens, historical figures, cultural symbols, and characteristic landscapes reveal the political and cultural heritage of different periods, as well as the development of postal systems. Beyond their collectible value, these stamps serve as fascinating visual records of history, artistic design, and cultural exchange between nations.

At CSO Gallery Hoi An, each stamp tells a miniature story of history, connecting the past and present through the unique imprints of the world.

In the historic town of Hoi An, Vietnam, a private collection has grown into a cultural space where history, literature, currency and world postal heritage come together.

CSO Gallery began with a passion for collecting — but collecting was only the beginning.

Over time, individual objects became collections. Collections became research. Research became stories. And those stories became an experience for visitors.

Today, CSO Gallery presents an extensive world of ancient currencies, stamps, Vietnamese cultural heritage and The Tale of Kieu, connecting Vietnam with stories from many countries and periods of history.

The Gallery's journey is rooted in one simple idea:

Collecting → Preserving → Researching → Storytelling → Educating.

I’ve been to quite a few museums, and most of the time they feel very grand and formal, with all these beautiful pieces displayed with information about where they came from, what they mean, when they were made, etc.

But this little museum in Hoi An felt so different to me.

Everything felt so personal. The clothes, accessories and other pieces weren’t just there as exhibits. They were displayed together with photographs of the actual people and communities they came from, and Réhahn himself had met and photographed many of them during his travels around Vietnam.

Even the descriptions beside the pieces didn’t feel like the usual museum plaques. They felt more like little stories about the people, how he met them, and the places he visited.

I don’t really know how to explain it properly, but walking through the museum almost felt like I was there with him when he met these people. Looking at the photographs, especially their faces and their eyes, somehow made me feel like I had met them too.

Out of all the museums I’ve visited, I don’t think I’ve ever experienced one that felt this intimate and human. I’m honestly not even a very sentimental person, but there were moments walking around where I genuinely felt a little emotional.

Such a small art gallery museum, but probably one of the most memorable ones I’ve visited.

Hoi An old town . The Phap Bao Pagoda, is located at 7 Hai Ba Trung Street in Hoi An.

On entering the grounds we were asked to don a light covering over our bare legs as a mark of respect.

The building and beautiful gardens are marvelous. It showcases traditional Vietnamese architecture with intricately carved wooden beams, majestic Buddha statues, and serene, colourful gardens.

The pagoda serves as a focal point for the local Buddhist community.

Then we rode through rice paddies to a local market to get the vegetables and herbs for the cooking class while enjoying street food snacks and drinks. This was one of the highlights of our stay in Hoi An. We had a wonderful experience, as it's more than just a cooking class. Our private tour started with a visit to a gorgeous organic vegetable farm where we got explanations about the herbs used in Vietnamese cooking. Normally this part is done by bike, but as we could not do this, the chef picked us up from our hotel with his car and drove us back and forth to the farm. After that we made a trip to a local market, where we got to try some local snacks and buy fresh ingredients for the class. Then we had the cooking class with delicious food, which we got to eat at the end of the class. We prepared 6 dishes. We learnt so much and will definitely be using the recipes, which the chef sent us by email, to cook at home! Definitely recommend this cooking class tour!!

I came for a class with my girlfriend and we had a great time. It was just the two of us in the class so it was easy to feel involved and relax. The tour in the morning was lots of fun and the food of course tasted great. We recieved copies of the recipe by email and I can't wait to try them when we get home.

It's also one of the first activities I've taken part in that didn't pressure us to buy more / write reviews etc so thank you for that :)

The cooking class is really amazing! Visiting the vegetable garden and the local market with the bicycle was lots of fun. After that we learned a lot about the vietnamese kitchen and how to prepare six simple but so delicious dishes with ingredients that you can also find at home, which is great. We also got the recipes and we’re looking forward to cook the meals at home. Thanks a lot for this wonderful experience!
Great teacher and amazing recipes! It’s a great experience, highly recommend

title: Viewpoint
address: XG65+PM, Cham Islands, Tân Hiệp, Quảng Nam, Vietnam

reviews.text:
Absolutely stunning viewpoint overlooking the entire main village on Cham Island!
This spot is pure magic - you get a panoramic view of the whole village, the harbor, and the surrounding turquoise waters. Perfect for photos, especially at sunset or golden hour. The scenery feels wild and untouched, exactly why I love exploring Cham Island.

Pro tip: The road leading up here is quite steep and narrow with some sharp turns, so ride carefully on your scooter (especially if it's raining or you're not used to Vietnamese mountain roads). Take it slow, use low gear, and enjoy the ride - it's worth every bit of effort.

Highly recommend detouring here if you're on the island. One of the best free viewpoints around. Bring water and your camera!
